title: Chapter 9 Quiz: WebSockets & Real-Time
description: Test your knowledge of WebSockets, connection management, broadcasting, and real-time applications.

questions.question: Which protocol upgrade is used to establish a WebSocket connection?
questions.explanation: A WebSocket connection starts as an HTTP request with `Upgrade: websocket` header.

questions.question: WebSockets are a request-response protocol like HTTP.
questions.explanation: WebSockets provide full-duplex, persistent communication where either side can send messages at any time.

questions.question: In FastAPI, how do you define a WebSocket endpoint?
questions.explanation: The `@app.websocket` decorator is used to register a WebSocket route.

questions.question: What method is called to accept an incoming WebSocket connection?
questions.explanation: `websocket.accept()` must be called to complete the handshake.

questions.question: Which exception is raised when a WebSocket client disconnects?
questions.explanation: `WebSocketDisconnect` is raised when the client closes the connection.

questions.question: You can use `await websocket.receive_json()` to get JSON data from the client.
questions.explanation: FastAPI provides convenience methods like `receive_json()` and `send_json()` for JSON messages.

questions.question: What is the purpose of storing active WebSocket connections in a list?
options: To send messages to all connected clients (broadcast)
To limit the number of connections
questions.explanation: Storing connections allows you to iterate over them and send messages (broadcast).

questions.question: What method is used to send a text message to a WebSocket client?
questions.explanation: `send_text(message)` sends a string to the client.

questions.question: What does broadcasting mean in the context of WebSockets?
options: Sending a message to a single client
Sending a message to all connected clients
Sending a message to the server
questions.explanation: Broadcasting sends the same message to every connected client.

questions.question: You can have multiple WebSocket endpoints in the same FastAPI app.
questions.explanation: Yes, you can define as many WebSocket routes as needed.

questions.question: How can you handle disconnections gracefully?
options: Wrap the receive loop in a try/except catching WebSocketDisconnect
Check connection status before each send
There is no way to detect disconnection
questions.explanation: Catching `WebSocketDisconnect` allows you to clean up and notify other clients.

questions.question: What is the recommended way to manage rooms in a chat application?
options: A dictionary mapping room names to lists of connections
A set of all connections with room metadata
questions.correctAnswer: A dictionary mapping room names to lists of connections
questions.explanation: This structure allows efficient per-room broadcasting.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common use case for WebSockets?
questions.explanation: WebSockets excel at real-time, server-initiated updates.

questions.question: WebSocket connections are automatically closed when the server restarts.
questions.explanation: WebSocket connections are tied to the server process; a restart will terminate them.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `WebSocketDisconnect` exception?
options: It indicates an error in the WebSocket protocol
It is raised when the client disconnects
It is raised when the server wants to disconnect
It is a normal part of the handshake
questions.explanation: `WebSocketDisconnect` is raised when the client closes the connection, allowing you to handle cleanup.

questions.question: What method do you use to send a binary message over WebSocket?
questions.explanation: `websocket.send_bytes(data)` sends binary data.

questions.question: In a chat application with multiple rooms, what should you do when a client disconnects?
options: Remove them from all rooms they were in
Do nothing, the connection will be garbage collected
Notify only that room about the departure
questions.explanation: You should remove the connection from the room and optionally notify other users in that room.

questions.question: You can use `await websocket.receive_json()` to receive a JSON object.
questions.explanation: `receive_json()` parses the incoming text as JSON and returns a Python object.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about WebSockets?
questions.explanation: WebSockets maintain a persistent connection, enabling real-time communication.

questions.question: What status code is returned when a WebSocket upgrade is successful?
questions.explanation: HTTP status code 101 indicates switching protocols.
